problem: Pricing, checkout and portal entitlement truth were split across different package names and commercial models, making it possible for website promises and runtime access to drift.
root_cause: The public pricing page evolved faster than the canonical SaaS plan and entitlement model, while consulting offers were not modeled alongside SaaS as one commercial catalog.
decision: Use one four-tier SaaS model (Starter, Pro, Groei, Enterprise) plus a separate consulting/workshop ladder, and project exact package limits into checkout and Portal V2 from server-side entitlements.
prevention: Every public SaaS promise must map to a canonical entitlement or explicit service inclusion.
Checkout plan codes must match active self-serve plan codes.
Portal V2 must show the authenticated organisation's package and effective limits from /api/portal-entitlements.
Consulting may grant temporary SaaS access, but does not silently change subscription truth.
Workshop or scan credit toward Build is a commercial rule and must remain explicit rather than hidden discount logic.
